_comment: How parts on the body plan's extension chains are generated, by the chain's name without its side (wings are generated on the left, "wing.L"; the right is the left's mirror). A part is pictured on its own as an object, like an isolated body part (see ISOLATED_STYLE in partgen.py, with "piece" naming what it is), steered by the depth of a plain stand-in along the chain at rest, made the brief's "length" in meters ("length" here, the rig's own chain length, by default): a tapered tube for a tail, a flat membrane for a wing (see tools/blender/test_extensions.py), seen from "view" ("front", "back" or "left", the character's left side) and turned "roll" degrees counterclockwise, so the part comes out in the chain's pose and proportions. "negative" adds to the negative prompt what the part tends to drag in, like the whole animal around a tail. "guideStrength" and "guideEnd" are how hard the stand-in's depth steers and for what share of the steps: lightly, since a stand-in is only a pose and a length, not a shape; a fox's brush or a feathered wing should spread well past it. "template" makes the part from a template shape and its picture, with no mesh (blender/fit_cape.py, for capes: a sheet hung from the shoulders "length" meters long, widening to "flare" times the shoulders at the hem, curving "wrap" meters round the sides, "offset" meters behind the chain and hung "clear" of the body), skipping meshes. Otherwise fitting (blender/fit_extension.py) lines the mesh up along the chain: "root" is the direction, in TRELLIS.2's space (+X the picture's right, +Y up, +Z toward the viewer), of the end that goes on the body; "line": "top" lines a wing up by its top edge, where its arm runs, rather than its middle, and "front" by its side nearest the camera, like a cape's back seen from behind; "bend": false only turns it rather than bending it along the chain, for a flat part; "offset" moves a part hanging off the body, like a cape, that many meters toward the camera from its chain, which runs inside the body, "behind" drops what lies more than that many meters toward the body's front from its chain, like the front panels of a cloak, and "clear" then pushes it that many meters off the body wherever it is nearer, like a collar over the shoulders; "onePiece" keeps only the biggest group of the mesh's loose pieces, for when TRELLIS.2 makes a pair of wings from one; "checkStreaks": false skips checking the mesh for curtains of streaks (see trellis_run.py), which a cape's long upright folds would look like; "keepThin" keeps thin spikes, which are otherwise dropped, like the pin a pictured tail stands on. "triangles" and "texture" are the fitted mesh's budget and texture size. A brief's "fit" replaces any of these.

tail.piece: a single detached tail on its own with no animal, seen from the side, hanging down and curving back
tail.negative: animal, whole animal, head, ears, legs, paws, torso, creature

cape.piece: a single long cape on its own with no person, seen from behind, hanging straight down from a collar
cape.negative: person, body, mannequin, head, arms, legs, hood up, sleeves

wing.piece: a single left wing, spread wide, seen from behind
